args.query: How big is the shadow tanker fleet carrying Russian crude, how does it avoid the price cap, and what enforcement has actually worked since 2024?

events.response_text:
Compiled research from Kestrel (3 pages):
[S1] Shadow Fleet Size Estimates: How Many Tankers, How Much Oil: How big the shadow tanker fleet is according to S&P Global, Lloyd's List Intelligence, KSE Institute and CREA, why their numbers differ so much, and what share of Russian seaborne crude it carries. For scale, market estimates put the non-sanctioned global crude and fuel tanker fleet at about 9,000 vessels.
[S2] The Oil Price Cap, Attestations and Insurance: How the G7/EU price cap on Russian seaborne oil works, how its level moved from $60 to $47.60 to $44.10, the attestation regime, and why insurance defines the shadow fleet. In June 2026, KSE counted 48 tankers with Russian insurance in the shadow fleet.
[S3] Enforcement: Vessel Designations, Inspections and Boardings: What the EU, UK and US have actually done to the shadow fleet since 2024: package-by-package vessel listings, the big US actions, Danish straits checks, boardings at sea, and which outcomes analysts can measure. In September 2026, sanctioned shadow tankers carried 67% of Russian crude (CREA).
Sources: shadow-fleet-size-estimates.md, price-cap-and-insurance.md, sanctions-enforcement.md
